passage: Leila Mansour and colleagues have explored how cross-regional maqam performance—a practice in which musicians from historically distinct musical traditions perform the same modal composition—can rely on a rhythmic framework shared by both traditions. Meanwhile, Haruki Tanaka and colleagues have investigated how such cross-regional performance proceeds through entirely distinct rhythmic frameworks, but the relative prevalence of cross-regional performance through shared and distinct rhythmic frameworks is still poorly understood. This motivated ethnomusicologists Deepak Mukherjee and Amira Cohen to evaluate both types of cross-regional performance in a single study for their 2015 paper.
prompt: According to the text, what did Mansour and colleagues focus on in their study?

choices.A: Cross-regional maqam performance arising from distinct rhythmic frameworks
choices.B: Cross-regional maqam performance arising from a shared rhythmic framework
choices.C: The performance of maqam compositions by musicians from the same musical tradition
choices.D: The relative prevalence of cross-regional performance emerging through shared and distinct rhythmic frameworks

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer because it presents information about Mansour and colleagues that is directly supported by the text. According to the text, Mansour and colleagues 'have explored how cross-regional maqam performance...can rely on a rhythmic framework shared by both traditions.'

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect because the text defines cross-regional maqam performance as 'a practice in which musicians from historically distinct musical traditions perform the same modal composition,' not musicians from the same tradition. The text indicates that Mansour and colleagues studied cross-regional performance, which by definition involves musicians from distinct traditions.
